:::{#def-local-minimizer}
#### Local minimizer

Let $A \subseteq \reals^p$
and let $f : A \to \reals$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function).
A point $x^* \in A$ is a **local minimizer** of $f$
if there is a number $\tolin > 0$
such that $f(x^*) \le f(x)$
for all $x \in A$ with
$\norm{x - x^*} < \tolin$,
where $\norm{\cdot}$ is the
[Euclidean norm](linear-algebra.qmd#def-euclidean-norm).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-local-minimizer}
#### Local and global minimizers

For $p = 1$, $\norm{x - x^*} = \abs{x - x^*}$.
For example, with $x^* = 1$ and $\tolin = 1$,
the condition $\abs{x - 1} < 1$ means $0 < x < 2$.

Every global minimizer (@def-global-minimizer) is a local minimizer:
take any $\tolin > 0$.
For example, $x^* = 0$ is a global minimizer of $f(x) = x^2$ on $\reals$,
so it is also a local minimizer.

The [converse](notation.qmd#def-converse) fails.
In @exr-local-vs-global-min,
$x^* = 1$ is a local minimizer of $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ (take $\tolin = 1$),
but not a global one.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#exm-not-local-minimizer}
#### A point that is not a local minimizer

For $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$, the point $x = -1$ is not a local minimizer.
For any $t$,

$$
\ba
f(-1 + t)
&= (-1 + t)^3 - 3(-1 + t)
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= (-1 + 3t - 3t^2 + t^3) - 3(-1 + t)
&& \text{(expand the cube)}
\\
&= -1 + 3t - 3t^2 + t^3 + 3 - 3t
&& \text{(multiply } -3 \text{ into the parentheses)}
\\
&= 2 - 3t^2 + t^3
&& \text{(} 3t - 3t = 0 \text{ and } -1 + 3 = 2 \text{)}
\\
&= 2 + t^2 (t - 3)
&& \text{(factor out } t^2 \text{)}
\\
&= f(-1) + t^2 (t - 3),
&& \text{(} f(-1) = (-1)^3 - 3(-1) \text{, which equals } 2 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and $t^2 (t - 3) < 0$ whenever $t \ne 0$ and $t < 3$.
So whatever $\tolin > 0$ is,
the point $x = -1 + t$ with $t = \min\cb{\tolin / 2, 1}$ satisfies $\abs{x - (-1)} < \tolin$
and $f(x) < f(-1)$.
For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(-0.9) &= -0.729 + 2.7 \\
&= 1.971 \\
&< 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#exm-not-local-minimizer}
#### A point that is not a local minimizer

For $f(x) = x^3 - 3x$, the point $x = -1$ is not a local minimizer.
For any $t$,

$$
\ba

&= (-1 + t)^3 - 3(-1 + t)

\\

\\

&& \text{(multiply } -3 \text{ into the parentheses)}
\ea

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{.theorem .example}

$$
\ba
f(-1 + t)
&= 2 - 3t^2 + t^3
&& \text{(} 3t - 3t = 0 \text{ and } -1 + 3 = 2 \text{)}
\\
&= 2 + t^2 (t - 3)
&& \text{(factor out } t^2 \text{)}
\\
&= f(-1) + t^2 (t - 3),
&& \text{(} f(-1) = (-1)^3 - 3(-1) \text{, which equals } 2 \text{)}
\ea

and $t^2 (t - 3) < 0$ whenever $t \ne 0$ and $t < 3$.
So whatever $\tolin > 0$ is,
the point $x = -1 + t$ with $t = \min\cb{\tolin / 2, 1}$ satisfies $\abs{x - (-1)} < \tolin$
and $f(x) < f(-1)$.
For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(-0.9) &= -0.729 + 2.7 \\
&= 1.971 \\
&< 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
